questions.q: A monochromatic light of frequency $5 \times 10^{14} \mathrm{~Hz}$ travelling through air, is incident on a medium of refractive index ' 2 '. Wavelength of the refracted light will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{f} \lambda=\mathrm{v} \quad \lambda_{\text {medium }}=\frac{\lambda_{\text {vacuum }}}{\mu}$
$\lambda_{\text {medium }} \Rightarrow \frac{3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 5 \times 10^{14}} \Rightarrow 0.3 \times 10^{-6} \Rightarrow 300 \mathrm{~nm}$

questions.solution:

Intensity of light after falling on polaroid C, IC=IAcos245°=I02cos245°=I04

Intensity of light after falling on polaroid B, IB=ICcos245°=I04cos245°=I08

questions.q: A light wave is propagating with plane wave fronts of the type $x+y+z=$ constant. The angle made by the direction of wave propagation with the $x$-axis is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The direction of propagation of light is perpendicular to the wave front and is symmetric about $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y}$ and z axis.
$\therefore$ Angle made by the light with $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \& \mathrm{z}$ axis is same.
$\therefore \quad \cos \alpha=\cos \beta=\cos \gamma(\alpha, \beta \& \gamma$ are angle made by light with $\mathrm{x}, \mathrm{y} \& \mathrm{z}$ axis respectively)
Also $\cos ^2 \alpha+\cos ^2 \beta+\cos ^2 \gamma=1$ [Sum of direction cosines]
$\therefore \alpha=\cos ^{-1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: In Young's double slits experiment, the position of 5<sup>th</sup> bright fringe from the central maximum is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The distance between slits and screen is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and wavelength of used monochromatic light is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>600</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math>. The separation between the slits is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, 

D=1 m, λ=600×10-9 m and n=5

Distance of nth bright fringe is given by, yn=nλDd, where, d is separation between the slits.

⇒5×600×10-9×1d=5×10-2

⇒d=5×600×10-9×15×10-2=60×10-6 m

⇒d=60 μm.

The phase difference between the beams is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi></math> at point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>. Then the difference between the resultant intensities at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Resultant intensity is given by, Iresultant=I1+I2+2I1I2cosϕ

At P, IP=9I+I+29I×Icosπ2=10I

At Q, IQ=9I+I+29I×Icosπ=10I-2×3I=4I

Now, difference between intensities is 10I-4I=6I

questions.q: ‘<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math>’ polarizing sheets are arranged such that each makes an angle <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> with the proceeding sheet. An unpolarized light of intensity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> is incident into this arrangement. The output intensity is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>I</mi><mn>64</mn></mfrac></math> . The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When an unpolarized light passes through a polariser, the intensity of the emergent light from the polariser depends on the square of the cosine of the angle between the plane of the polariser and the direction of the incident light.

The formula to calculate the intensity I1 of the emergent light from a polariser which makes an angle θ with the direction of the incident light is given by

I1= Icos2θ..................(1)

where, I is the intensity of the incident light.

Substitute 45° for θ into equation (1) to obtain the intensity of the first emergent light.

I1= Icos245°= I2

In a similar manner, the intensity I2 of the second emergent light can be written as

I2= I1cos245°= I12= I4=I22

Thus, for n number of such polarisers, the net intensity In of the emergent light can be written as

In= I2n......................(1)

Comparing equation (1) with the given expression for the intensity, it can be concluded that

n= 6

questions.q:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion-(A) : If Young's double slit experiment is performed in an optically denser medium than air, then the consecutive fringes come closer.
Reason-(R) : The speed of light reduces in an optically denser medium than air while its frequency does not change.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true but $(\mathbf{R})$ is not the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\beta(\text { fringe width })=\frac{\lambda D}{d}$

In denser medium, $\lambda \downarrow \Rightarrow \beta \downarrow\Rightarrow$ fringe come closer

Also, $\mu=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mathrm{V}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{V}=\frac{\mathrm{c}}{\mu}$
Frequency remains same,
$\Rightarrow \mu=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{vac} .} \mathrm{f}}{\lambda_{\mathrm{med}} \mathrm{f}} \Rightarrow \lambda_{\mathrm{med}}=\frac{\lambda_{\mathrm{vac} .}}{\mu}$

questions.q: Two beams of light having intensities <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>I</mi></math> interfere to produce a fringe pattern on a screen. The phase difference between the two beams are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>3</mn></mfrac></math> at points <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> respectively. The difference between the resultant intensities at the two points is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mi>I</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, phase difference at point A and B are ϕA=π2and ϕB=π3.

Resultant intensity at point A, 

IA=I+4I+2I4Icosπ2

⇒IA=5I+4I0=5I

Resultant intensity at point B,

IB=I+4I+2I4Icos60° =5I+4I×12=7I

Difference in intensities is IB-IA=7I-5I=2I.

Thus, value of x=2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The distance between nth bright fringe on both side of central maxima is 2.4 cm. The f=?

Δy=Dλd×8
λ=dΔy8D=0.3×10-3×2.4×10-28×1.5=0.12×10-52=0.06×10-5
λ=6×10-7 m
f=C6×10-7=0.5×10+15
f=5×1014 Hz
So, x=5

questions.q: A parallel beam of monochromatic light of wavelength $600 \mathrm{~nm}$ passes through single slit of $0.4 \mathrm{~mm}$ width. Angular divergence corresponding to second order minima would be ______ $\times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\sin \theta \simeq \theta \simeq \frac{2 \lambda}{b}=\frac{2 \times 600 \times 10^{-9}}{4 \times 10^{-4}}=3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$
Total divergence $=(3+3) \times 10^{-3}=6 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{rad}$

questions.q: As shown in figures, three identical polaroids P1, P2 and P3 are placed one after another. The pass axis of P2 and P3 are inclined at angle of 60º and 90º with respect to axis of P1. The source S has an intensity of 256 W m-2. The intensity of light at point O is _____W m-2.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As given here, the pass axis of P2 and P3 are inclined at angle of 60º and 90º with respect to axis of P1. 

Therefore, intensity of light after falling on first polaroid P1, I1=I02

Intensity of light after falling on second polaroid P2, I2=I1cos260°=I08

Intensity of light after falling on third polaroid P3, I3=I2cos230°=I0834=3I032

The intensity of light at O is 3I032=3×25632=24 W m-2
